meaning: Laughing in a loud, harsh way, like a witch; also the sound a hen makes
hindi: कर्कश हँसी हँसते हुए; मुर्गी का कुड़कुड़ाना
trick: A witch CACKLING over her pot: 'heh-heh-heh!'

We heard the hens cackling in the yard.

meaning: The rise and fall of the voice or a rhythm in speech or music

examples: She speaks with a gentle cadence.
The song has a slow, steady cadence.

trick: CADRES: the core CADRE of a team, the trained insiders.
examples: The party trained new cadres in every village.
Army cadres led the training.

Her face was caked in makeup.

meaning: Criticised someone publicly for doing something wrong (past); also shouted something

Her feet were calloused from walking barefoot.

The soldiers shared a strong camaraderie.

meaning: (Informal) Short for camouflage: clothing with green and brown patterns

examples: He wore camo pants on the hike.
She bought a camo jacket.

meaning: Hidden by colours or patterns that match the surroundings (past)

The tanks were camouflaged with branches.

meaning: Being honest and open in what you say
trick: CANDOR = CANDID talk: no hiding.
examples: I appreciate your candor.
She spoke with surprising candor about her mistakes.

meaning: A round metal container with a lid
trick: CANISTER: a CAN with a lid.
examples: Keep the tea in a metal canister.
The firefighters carried oxygen canisters.

meaning: Italian fried pastry tubes filled with sweet creamy cheese

examples: We bought cannoli from the Italian bakery.
The cannoli were crispy and sweet.

meaning: A cover hung over something; also the top layer of branches in a forest

examples: The bed has a white canopy.
Monkeys live in the forest canopy.

meaning: Changing mood or behaviour suddenly and without reason

meaning: (Of a boat) turned upside down in the water (past)

Strong waves capsized the canoe.

trick: CARCASS: a CAR hit it, now it's a dead CASE.

The carcass of a deer lay on the road.

meaning: The violent killing of many people
trick: CARNAGE: CARNage = flesh (carne) everywhere.
examples: The bomb caused terrible carnage.
Pictures of the carnage shocked the world.

meaning: A vehicle pulled by horses; also a train coach
trick: CARRIAGE CARRIES people.
examples: The queen rode in a golden carriage.
Our train carriage was full.

meaning: People who make maps
trick: CARTO = map (like 'chart') + GRAPH = draw: map drawers.
examples: Old cartographers drew maps by hand.
Cartographers use satellite photos to make maps today.

meaning: A small plastic box with tape for recording music or sound (old)
hindi: कैसेट, गाने की टेप वाली डिब्बी
trick: CASSETTE: a small CASE of tape.
examples: Dad still has his old music cassettes.
She recorded the song on a cassette.

meaning: A list or book of items, for example things to buy; also to make such a list
trick: CATALOG: a list of everything, even CATS for sale.
examples: I looked through the shopping catalog.
They catalog every book in the library.

usage.pattern: a catalog of something; catalog something

meaning: A small worm-like creature that turns into a butterfly
trick: CATERPILLAR: a hairy CAT-like PILLow that crawls.
examples: The caterpillar ate the leaves.
A caterpillar becomes a butterfly.

usage.pattern: a caterpillar turns into a butterfly

meaning: Releasing strong emotions in a way that makes you feel better
hindi: मन का गुबार निकलना, भावनाओं का निकास
trick: CATHARSIS: crying it out and feeling clean after.
examples: Writing in her diary was a kind of catharsis.
The sad film gave me a catharsis.

meaning: A thin tube put into the body to remove or add liquids
hindi: शरीर में डाली जाने वाली पतली नली
trick: CATHETER: a hospital tube.
examples: The nurse put in a catheter.
He had a catheter after the operation.

meaning: A large round metal pot for cooking over a fire
trick: A witch's CAULDRON bubbling over the fire.
examples: The witch stirred her cauldron.
Soup boiled in a big cauldron.

meaning: Fell in or collapsed; also gave in after pressure (past)
hindi: धँस गया, ढह गया; झुक गया, हार मान ली
trick: The CAVE roof CAVED in; you CAVED and said yes.
examples: The roof caved in during the storm.
He caved and bought her the toy.

meaning: Large natural holes in the side of a hill or under the ground
trick: Bats live in CAVES.
examples: We explored the caves near the beach.
Bats sleep in dark caves.

meaning: Giving in after pressure; also collapsing; also exploring caves as a hobby
hindi: दबाव में झुकना, हार मानना; ढहना; गुफाओं की सैर
trick: CAVE-ing: falling in like a CAVE roof.
examples: Stop caving to every request.
We went caving in the mountains.

meaning: A tall evergreen tree with sweet-smelling wood
trick: CEDAR wood smells sweet in a chest.
examples: The box is made of cedar.
A tall cedar stood by the house.

meaning: A grey powder mixed with water and sand to build things; also to make something stronger
trick: CEMENT holds bricks together; it can also CEMENT a friendship.
examples: The workers mixed cement for the new wall.
The trip helped cement their friendship.

usage.pattern: cement something (a friendship / a place / a deal)

meaning: A place where dead people are buried
trick: CEMETERY: spelt with three E's: cEmEtEry.
examples: My grandparents are buried in this cemetery.
We walked past the old cemetery.

meaning: To rub and make sore; also to feel annoyed by rules
trick: CHAFE: rough cloth rubbing your skin.
examples: These new shoes chafe my feet.
He began to chafe under the strict rules.

meaning: Rubbed and made sore; also felt annoyed by limits (past)
trick: CHAFED: the skin got rubbed raw.
examples: The strap chafed her shoulder.
He chafed at being told what to do.

meaning: Rubbing that makes skin sore; also being annoyed by limits
trick: CHAFING: legs rubbing on a long walk.
examples: Running in wet clothes can cause chafing.
She was chafing at the slow progress.

usage.pattern: prevent chafing; be chafing at something

meaning: Wrote or drew with chalk (past); chalked up = achieved or explained something as caused by
hindi: खड़िया से लिखा; श्रेय दिया, हासिल किया
trick: CHALKED it on the board.
examples: The kids chalked pictures on the road.
She chalked up another win.

usage.pattern: chalk something (on something); chalk up something; chalk something up to something

meaning: A TV station; a passage for water; also to direct energy or feelings into something
trick: CHANNEL water into a field, CHANNEL your anger into sport.
examples: Change the channel, this show is boring.
She channels her stress into running.

meaning: Having a strong, attractive personality that makes people like and follow you
trick: CHARISMA = charm; CHARISMATIC people CHARM everyone.
examples: Our new manager is very charismatic.
The charismatic singer had the crowd cheering.

meaning: Scolding or criticising someone strongly
trick: CHASTISE: CHASE them with angry words.
examples: The teacher was chastising the noisy boys.
Stop chastising yourself for one mistake.

usage.pattern: chastise someone for something / for doing something

meaning: (Informal) Short for chemistry, the school subject
trick: CHEM = CHEMistry class.
examples: I have a chem test tomorrow.
Our chem teacher is very strict.

meaning: To slowly make something smaller or weaker, a little bit at a time
hindi: धीरे-धीरे कम करना, थोड़ा-थोड़ा कमज़ोर करना
trick: Like a sculptor CHIPPING AWAY AT stone, one little piece at a time.
examples: I'm chipping away at my homework a bit every day.
Small lies chip away at trust.

meaning: Having sharp, strong features as if carved; also cut with a chisel (past)
hindi: तराशा हुआ, सुडौल; छेनी से काटा
trick: CHISELED like a statue carved with a CHISEL.
examples: The actor has a chiseled jaw.
He chiseled his name into the wood.

usage.pattern: a chiseled + noun (jaw / face); chisel something into something

meaning: Couldn't breathe because something blocked the throat; also failed under pressure (past)
hindi: दम घुटा, गला रुँधा; दबाव में चूक गया
trick: CHOKED: the throat closed up, or you froze in the big moment.
examples: He choked on a fish bone.
The player choked in the final.

meaning: Couldn't breathe because something was stuck in the throat (past)
hindi: गले में अटकने से दम घुटा
trick: CHOKED ON food: it got stuck and you couldn't breathe.
examples: The baby choked on a small piece of apple.
He choked on his coffee when he heard the news.

meaning: A boring job you have to do regularly, like housework
hindi: रोज़ का घरेलू काम, उबाऊ काम
trick: CHORE: CHOre = a job you do but don't enjoy.
examples: Washing the dishes is my least favourite chore.
Kids should help with chores.

meaning: Picked from a group (past participle of choose)
trick: CHOOSE → CHOSE → CHOSEN.
examples: She was chosen as the team captain.
Have you chosen a dress for the party?

usage.pattern: be chosen (as/for something); have chosen something

meaning: (Informal) Food; chow down = eat a lot
trick: CHOW sounds like CHOW mein: food!
examples: Let's get some chow.
The kids chowed down on pizza.

meaning: A quiet, soft laugh; also to laugh quietly
trick: CHUCKLE: a small 'chuck-chuck' laugh.
examples: He gave a little chuckle at the joke.
She chuckled while reading the message.

usage.pattern: chuckle at/about something; give a chuckle

meaning: Moved or stirred violently; also (stomach) felt sick from nerves (past)
hindi: मथा, उथल-पुथल हुई; पेट में मरोड़ उठी
trick: Butter is CHURNED by stirring hard.
examples: The sea churned in the storm.
My stomach churned before the exam.

meaning: A slide or tube for sending things down; also short for parachute
trick: CHUTE: things SHOOT down it.
examples: Throw the rubbish down the chute.
The kids slid down the water chute.

usage.pattern: a chute (for something); down the chute

meaning: Slides or tubes for sending things down (plural); also parachutes
trick: One CHUTE, two CHUTES: Snakes and Ladders = Chutes and Ladders.
examples: The water park has three big chutes.
We played Chutes and Ladders.

meaning: Tightened something like a belt around the waist; also made sure of something (past)
trick: CINCHED the belt: tight and SECURE (a cinch).
examples: She cinched her coat with a belt.
That goal cinched the win.

meaning: A large grey building block made of concrete and ashes
trick: CINDER (ashes) + BLOCK.
examples: The garage has cinderblock walls.
He used a cinderblock to hold the door open.

meaning: Long and indirect; not going the straight way
trick: Like a CIRCUIT: you go round and round instead of straight.
examples: We took a circuitous route to avoid traffic.
He gave a circuitous answer instead of saying no.

meaning: The facts or conditions that affect a situation
trick: CIRCUM = around: things AROUND a situation.
examples: Under these circumstances, we should wait.

usage.pattern: under/in the circumstances; under no circumstances

meaning: Shouted or demanded something loudly together (past)
hindi: शोर मचाया, ज़ोर से माँग की
trick: CLAMOR = loud CLAMOUR of a crowd.
examples: The fans clamored for an autograph.
The children clamored to see the puppy.

usage.pattern: clamor for something / to do something

meaning: Done secretly, often because it is not allowed
trick: CLANDESTINE: a CLAN meeting in secret.
examples: They had a clandestine meeting at night.
The spy ran a clandestine operation.

meaning: A loud ringing sound of metal hitting metal
trick: CLANG! A pot dropped on the floor.
examples: The gate shut with a loud clang.
The pans clanged in the kitchen.

meaning: Afraid of small closed spaces; also (of a place) small and crowded
hindi: बंद जगह से डरने वाला; तंग, घुटन भरा

examples: I feel claustrophobic in lifts.
The tiny room was claustrophobic.

meaning: Official permission; also the removal of things; also the space above or around something
hindi: मंज़ूरी, अनुमति; हटाना, सफ़ाई; खाली जगह
trick: CLEARANCE: you're CLEARED to go.
examples: The plane got clearance to land.
Everything is half price in the clearance sale.

usage.pattern: get clearance (to do something); clearance sale

meaning: A split or opening in something, like a cleft chin
trick: CLEFT = CLEFT apart, a split.
examples: He has a cleft in his chin.
Water ran through a cleft in the rock.

meaning: Related to office work like typing and filing; also related to priests
trick: CLERK + ical: CLERK work in an office.
examples: She has a clerical job at the bank.
It was just a clerical error in the form.

meaning: All the customers of a shop, hotel or business
trick: CLIENT-ELE: all the CLIENTS together.
examples: The café has a young clientele.
The hotel's clientele is mostly tourists.

meaning: To hold on tightly; also to stay close or attached
trick: CLING like CLING film sticking to a bowl.
examples: The baby monkey clings to its mother.
Don't cling to the past.

meaning: Measuring time or speed; clocking in = recording when you start work; also (informal) noticing
hindi: समय या गति नापना; हाज़िरी दर्ज करना; भाँप लेना (बोलचाल)
trick: CLOCKING: putting time on the CLOCK.
examples: The car was clocking 120 km/h.
Workers are clocking in for the morning shift.

usage.pattern: clock in/out; clock up something; clock someone/something

meaning: To block something so nothing can pass; also a wooden shoe
hindi: रुकावट डालना, जाम करना; लकड़ी का जूता, खड़ाऊँ
trick: CLOG the drain with hair.
examples: Don't pour oil down the sink, it will clog the pipe.
She wore wooden clogs in the garden.

meaning: Blocked so that nothing can pass
trick: CLOGGED drain: water won't go down.
examples: The sink is clogged again.
The roads were clogged with traffic.

meaning: Blocking something so nothing can move through
hindi: जाम करते हुए, रुकावट डालते हुए

examples: Leaves are clogging the gutter.
Cars were clogging the street.

meaning: A performer with a painted face who does funny things; also a silly person
trick: The CLOWN at the circus with a red nose.
examples: The kids laughed at the clown.
Stop acting like a clown in class.

usage.pattern: clown around; act like a clown

meaning: Heavy, awkward and old-fashioned; also badly done
trick: CLUNKY: it goes CLUNK when you move it.
examples: He still uses a clunky old laptop.
The website is slow and clunky.

meaning: Held something tightly, often because of fear or worry (past)
trick: CLUTCHED like holding on to a CLUTCH bag tightly.
examples: She clutched her bag on the crowded train.
He clutched his chest in pain.

meaning: Holding something tightly
trick: CLUTCHING: hands squeezed tight around it.
examples: The child was clutching her teddy bear.
He walked in clutching a bunch of flowers.

usage.pattern: be clutching something; clutch at something

meaning: Turning from liquid into a thick, semi-solid form (like blood clotting)
trick: CO-AG-ULATING: liquid GLUING together into lumps.
examples: The blood was coagulating around the cut.
The milk is coagulating because it's gone bad.

meaning: The land next to the sea; also to move easily without effort
hindi: तट, किनारा; बिना मेहनत आगे बढ़ना

examples: We drove along the coast.
He's just coasting through school.

meaning: (Informal) Too confident in an annoying way
trick: COCKY like a proud rooster (cock) strutting around.
examples: Don't get cocky just because you won once.
The cocky player lost the match.

meaning: Treats someone too gently and protectively
hindi: लाड़-प्यार करता है, ज़रूरत से ज़्यादा सँभालता है

examples: She coddles her son like a baby.
The coach never coddles his players.

meaning: Clear, logical and convincing
trick: COGENT: the argument has all its COGS working.
examples: She made a cogent argument for the plan.
He gave a cogent reason for being late.

meaning: Related to thinking, learning and understanding
trick: COGNITIVE = COG-nitive: the brain's COGS turning.

meaning: To fit together well as a clear whole; also to stick together

The team began to cohere after a few weeks.

meaning: The punctuation mark (:); also the main part of the large intestine
trick: COLON: two dots, one on top of the other.
examples: Use a colon before a list.
The doctor checked his colon.

usage.pattern: use a colon; the colon (body part)

meaning: Ready and eager to fight or argue
trick: COMBAT-ive: always ready for COMBAT.
examples: He gets combative when he's tired.
She has a combative style in debates.

meaning: Bright objects in space with long glowing tails (plural)
trick: COMETS COME with a tail of light.
examples: We watched comets through the telescope.
Comets have long, bright tails.

meaning: To take something for your own use by force or authority
trick: COMMANDEER: COMMAND it to be yours.
examples: The police commandeered a car to chase the thief.
My brother commandeered the TV remote.

meaning: Rules that must be obeyed, especially the Ten Commandments in the Bible
trick: COMMANDS from God: the Ten COMMANDMENTS.
examples: Moses received the Ten Commandments.
My mom has her own commandments for the house.

usage.pattern: the Ten Commandments; obey/follow the commandments

meaning: To praise someone formally; also to recommend
hindi: सराहना करना, प्रशंसा करना; सिफ़ारिश करना
trick: COMMEND sounds like reCOMMEND: speak well of someone.
examples: The teacher commended her for her hard work.
I commend your honesty.

usage.pattern: commend someone for something / for doing something

meaning: A group of people living together and sharing everything; also to feel close to (commune with nature)
trick: COMMUNE = COMMUNity living together.
examples: They lived in a commune in the hills.
He goes hiking to commune with nature.

usage.pattern: live in a commune; commune with something

meaning: To separate things into parts; also to keep thoughts or feelings separate
hindi: अलग-अलग खानों में बाँटना; विचारों को अलग रखना
trick: COMPARTMENT-alize: put each thing in its own COMPARTMENT.
examples: She can compartmentalize work and home life.
Try to compartmentalize your worries.

meaning: Feeling too pleased with yourself so you stop trying
trick: COMPLACENCY: being in a COMfy PLACE and getting lazy.
examples: Complacency can lose you the match.
There's no room for complacency at work.

meaning: Calm and in control of your feelings; also written or made up of (past)
hindi: शांत, संयत; रचा गया, बना हुआ
trick: COMPOSED: all your pieces are in place, so you stay calm.
examples: She stayed composed during the interview.
The team is composed of five players.

usage.pattern: stay composed; be composed of something

meaning: Unable to stop doing something; also very interesting (compulsive viewing)
hindi: आदत से मजबूर, बाध्यकारी; बेहद दिलचस्प
trick: COMPULSIVE: you feel COMPELLED to do it.
examples: He's a compulsive liar.
The show was compulsive viewing.

meaning: To admit that something is true, often unwillingly; also to give up
hindi: मान लेना, स्वीकार करना; हार मान लेना
trick: CONCEDE = give in, like conceding a goal.
examples: He finally conceded that he was wrong.
The team conceded two goals.

usage.pattern: concede that ...; concede something (a goal / defeat)

meaning: Possible to imagine or believe
trick: CONCEIVE an idea = CONCEIVABLE: you can imagine it.
examples: It's conceivable that he forgot.
We tried every conceivable way.

usage.pattern: it is conceivable that ...; every conceivable + noun

meaning: A live music performance
trick: CONCERT: everyone sings in CONCERT (together).
examples: We went to a rock concert.
The concert starts at seven.

usage.pattern: go to a concert; at a concert

meaning: Made up a story or excuse; also mixed something new from different things (past)
hindi: गढ़ा, मनगढ़ंत बनाया; मिलाकर तैयार किया
trick: CONCOCTED: COOKED up an excuse.
examples: He concocted a story about a lost bus.
She concocted a drink from fruit and mint.

usage.pattern: concoct something (a story / a plan / a dish)

meaning: A head injury that makes you confused or unconscious for a while
trick: CONCUSSION: a CRUSH to the head.
examples: He got a concussion playing football.
Rest is important after a concussion.

meaning: Acting as if you are better or smarter than others
trick: CONDESCENDING: looking DOWN (descending) on people.
examples: I hate his condescending tone.
She was condescending to the new staff.

meaning: Words of sympathy for someone whose loved one has died
trick: CONDOLENCES = CON (with) + DOLE (sorrow): sharing their sorrow.
examples: Please accept my condolences.
We sent our condolences to the family.

meaning: To tell someone a secret or private feelings because you trust them
trick: CONFIDE: tell someone you have CONFIDENCE in.
examples: She confided in her best friend.
He confided that he was scared.

usage.pattern: confide in someone; confide (to someone) that ...

meaning: To keep someone or something within limits or in a small space
trick: CON-FINE: kept inside FINE borders.
examples: Please confine your answer to 100 words.
The sick dog was confined to the house.

usage.pattern: confine someone/something to something; be confined to something

meaning: An angry argument or fight between people or groups
trick: CONFRONT = face someone; a CONFRONTATION is face-to-face fighting.
examples: He wanted to avoid a confrontation with his boss.
There was a confrontation between police and protesters.

meaning: Becoming thick or solid as it cools, like fat or blood
trick: CONGEALING: CON + GEL: turning into jelly.
examples: The fat was congealing in the pan.
Her blood was congealing around the cut.

meaning: Too much traffic or too many people; also a blocked nose or chest
hindi: भीड़-भाड़, जाम; नाक या छाती में जकड़न
trick: CONGESTION: everything is JAMMED in.
examples: There's heavy congestion on the highway.
This medicine helps with nasal congestion.

meaning: A group of people gathered for worship in a church
trick: CONGREGATE = gather; the CONGREGATION gathers in church.
examples: The priest spoke to the congregation.
The whole congregation sang together.

meaning: To make something appear as if by magic; also to bring a picture to mind
hindi: जादू से प्रकट करना; मन में तस्वीर लाना
trick: A magician CONJURES a rabbit from a hat.
examples: The magician conjured a rabbit out of his hat.
The song conjures memories of summer.

usage.pattern: conjure something (up); conjure up an image/memory

meaning: Made something appear as if by magic; also brought to mind (past)
hindi: जादू से प्रकट किया; याद दिलाया
trick: CONJURED: like a magic trick.
examples: She conjured a meal from leftovers.
The smell conjured up childhood memories.

meaning: General agreement among a group
trick: CONSENSUS: everyone's SENSE is the same.
examples: The team reached a consensus.
There is no consensus on the plan.

meaning: Comforted someone who was sad (past)
trick: CONSOLED: like a game CONSOLE cheers up a sad kid.
examples: She consoled her crying friend.
He consoled himself with ice cream.

usage.pattern: console someone; console yourself with something

meaning: Having difficulty emptying your bowels
trick: CONSTIPATED: things are STUCK.
examples: Eat more fibre if you feel constipated.
The baby was constipated for two days.

meaning: Helpful and useful, meant to improve something
trick: CONSTRUCT = build; CONSTRUCTIVE feedback helps you build better.
examples: Thanks for the constructive feedback.
Let's have a constructive discussion.

meaning: To understand or explain words or actions in a particular way
trick: CONSTRUE: how you CONSTRUCT the meaning in your head.
examples: His silence was construed as agreement.
Don't construe my advice as criticism.

meaning: Spreading from one person to another, like a disease or a feeling
trick: CONTAGIOUS: it spreads by CONTACT.
examples: Flu is very contagious.
Her laugh is so contagious!

meaning: To think deeply about something for a long time; also to consider doing something
trick: CONTEMPLATE: sit in a TEMPLE and think.
examples: He sat by the lake to contemplate life.
She is contemplating a move to Delhi.

meaning: A feeling that someone or something is worthless or doesn't deserve respect
trick: CONTEMPT: you look at it with a CON-TEMPTed sneer.
examples: She looked at him with contempt.
He has contempt for lazy people.

meaning: To compete for something; also to argue that something is true; contend with = deal with a problem
hindi: मुक़ाबला करना; दावा करना; जूझना, निपटना
trick: CONTEND: CONTEST + DEFEND.
examples: Four teams contend for the cup.
We have to contend with heavy traffic.

usage.pattern: contend for something; contend with something; contend that ...

meaning: A disagreement or argument; also an opinion someone argues for
trick: CONTENTION: the point of CONTEST.
examples: Money is a point of contention between them.
Our team is in contention for the trophy.

usage.pattern: a point/bone of contention; in contention (for something)

meaning: Possible future events you plan for in case they happen
trick: CONTINGENCIES: plans that CONTINue if things go wrong.
examples: We have money saved for contingencies.
The plan covers all contingencies.

meaning: Caught a disease; also became smaller; also made a legal agreement (past)
hindi: बीमारी लगी; सिकुड़ गया; अनुबंध किया
trick: CONTRACT a disease, a muscle CONTRACTS, sign a CONTRACT.
examples: He contracted malaria on his trip.
The metal contracted in the cold.

usage.pattern: contract a disease; something contracted; be contracted to do something

meaning: Opposite; also (of a person) liking to disagree
hindi: विपरीत, उल्टा; ज़िद्दी, विरोधी स्वभाव का
trick: CONTRA = against: the CONTRARY is the opposite.
examples: On the contrary, I loved the film.
Contrary to what you think, I'm not angry.

usage.pattern: contrary to something; on the contrary

meaning: Getting better slowly after an illness
hindi: ठीक होते हुए, स्वास्थ्य लाभ करते हुए
trick: CONVALESCING: in a VALLEY of rest, healing slowly.
examples: He is convalescing at home after surgery.
She spent a month convalescing by the sea.

meaning: Came together from different directions to meet at one point (past)
hindi: एक जगह आकर मिले, एकत्र हुए
trick: CON-VERGE: all lines move to the same VERGE (edge/point).
examples: The two roads converged near the river.
Thousands of fans converged on the stadium.

meaning: A strong belief; also a court decision that someone is guilty
trick: CONVICTION: you're CONVINCED; a CONVICT has a conviction.
examples: She spoke with great conviction.
He has a previous conviction for theft.

usage.pattern: with conviction; a conviction for something

meaning: A tall plant with yellow seeds that we eat; also the seeds themselves
trick: CORN on the cob, popcorn!
examples: We ate grilled corn by the beach.
Popcorn is made from corn.

meaning: The most important part that everything else is based on; also a stone at the corner of a building
trick: The CORNER STONE holds up the whole building.
examples: Trust is the cornerstone of a good friendship.
Education is the cornerstone of success.

meaning: Gathered people or animals together into one place (past)
trick: A CORRAL is a pen; CORRALLED = rounded up into it.
examples: The teacher corralled the kids into the bus.
The cowboys corralled the horses.

meaning: Long passages in a building with doors to rooms (plural)
trick: CORRIDORS: long halls you RUN down.
examples: The hospital corridors were quiet.
Don't run in the school corridors.

meaning: Slowly damaged or worn away, especially by rust or chemicals (past)
trick: CORRODED: the metal was eaten by ROT and rust.
examples: The old pipes were corroded with rust.
Lies slowly corroded their trust.

meaning: A hormone the body releases when you are stressed
trick: CORTISOL: the stress hormone that puts your body on ALERT.
examples: Stress raises cortisol levels.
Sleep helps lower cortisol.

meaning: To sign a document together with someone, promising to pay if they don't
trick: CO-SIGN: sign it TOGETHER.
examples: My dad had to cosign my car loan.
Will you cosign the lease with me?

meaning: Expressed in a particular way or style (past); also lying down (old)
hindi: शब्दों में ढाला, व्यक्त किया; लेटा हुआ
trick: COUCHED: wrapped words in soft COUCH cushions.
examples: The warning was couched in polite language.
His request was couched as a joke.

meaning: To reduce or stop the effect of something by doing the opposite
trick: COUNTER-ACT: ACT against it.
examples: Drink water to counteract the heat.
The medicine counteracts the poison.

meaning: Different from what you would naturally expect
trick: COUNTER (against) + INTUITIVE (your gut feeling): against your gut.
examples: It sounds counterintuitive, but resting makes you faster.
The answer to the puzzle was counterintuitive.

meaning: Flowing quickly (of a liquid or feeling)
trick: Like a river running its COURSE fast.
examples: Tears were coursing down her cheeks.
He felt the energy coursing through his body.

meaning: Wanted very much, especially something that belongs to someone else (past / adjective)
trick: COVETED: you want it so much you'd COVER it with your hands.
examples: She won the coveted award.
He coveted his neighbour's car.

meaning: To bend down or move back because you are afraid
trick: COWER like a scared COW hiding.
examples: The dog cowered in the corner during the storm.
Don't cower, stand up for yourself.

meaning: Broken with lines on the surface but not in pieces; also solved; also (informal) crazy (past)
hindi: चटक गया, दरार पड़ी; हल कर लिया; पागल (बोलचाल)
trick: CRACKED: the phone screen has lines on it.
examples: My phone screen is cracked.
The police cracked the case.

meaning: Made a series of short, sharp popping sounds, like a fire (past)
trick: CRACK-CRACK: the fire CRACKLED.
examples: The fire crackled in the fireplace.
The radio crackled and went silent.

meaning: Holding gently and carefully in your arms
hindi: प्यार से गोद में थामे हुए
trick: Like rocking a baby in a CRADLE.
examples: She was cradling the baby in her arms.
He sat cradling a cup of hot tea.

meaning: Studying a lot in a very short time; also pushing too many things into a space
trick: CRAMMING: stuffing your brain like a full suitcase.
examples: She's cramming for her exam tomorrow.
He was cramming clothes into his bag.

usage.pattern: cram for something; cram something into something

meaning: Metal spikes fixed to boots for walking on ice or snow
hindi: बर्फ़ पर चलने के लिए जूतों के नुकीले काँटे
trick: CRAMPONS: CRAMP your boots onto the ice.
examples: Climbers wear crampons on icy mountains.
He tied the crampons to his boots.

meaning: Stretched your neck to see something better (past)
trick: Like a CRANE bird stretching its long neck.
examples: She craned her neck to see the stage.
People craned to see the singer.

meaning: (Informal, a bit rude) Of very bad quality
trick: CRAP-py: as bad as rubbish.
examples: I had a crappy day at work.
This crappy phone keeps breaking.

meaning: A line made by folding or crushing paper or cloth; also to make such a line
trick: CREASE: the line when you fold a shirt.
examples: Iron out the creases in your shirt.
Don't crease the letter.

usage.pattern: a crease in something; crease something

meaning: A set of beliefs, especially religious
trick: CREED: what you believe and NEED to follow.
examples: People of every creed are welcome.
Honesty is his creed.

usage.pattern: race, colour or creed; someone's creed

meaning: Small streams or narrow rivers (plural)
trick: CREEKS: little streams that CREAK over stones.
examples: The kids played in the creeks behind the farm.
Creeks run down the hill after rain.

meaning: Moved slowly and quietly (past of creep)
trick: CREEP → CREPT, like SLEEP → SLEPT.
examples: She crept into the room so she wouldn't wake him.
Doubt crept into his mind.

meaning: A gradual increase in loudness; also the loudest or most intense point
trick: CRESCENDO: the music climbs up to the top.
examples: The music rose to a crescendo.
The cheers reached a crescendo.

meaning: The top of a hill or wave; also a family or school symbol
trick: CREST: the top of the wave, like a bird's head crest.
examples: We stopped at the crest of the hill.
The school crest is on our blazer.

usage.pattern: the crest of something; on the crest of a wave
partners: on the crest of a wave

meaning: Reached the top of a hill or wave (past); also having a crest (like a crested bird)
trick: CRESTED: got to the top CREST.
examples: We crested the hill and saw the sea.
The crested bird had bright feathers.

meaning: A small fold or wrinkle; also to form small folds or wrinkles
trick: CRINKLE: the crunchy sound of wrapping paper.
examples: Her eyes crinkle when she smiles.
He heard the crinkle of a chip packet.

meaning: Damages something or someone so badly it can't work properly; also (offensive, old) people who can't walk well
hindi: पंगु बना देता है, नाकारा कर देता है; अपंग लोग (लोगों के लिए अपमानजनक)
trick: CRIPPLES: breaks the legs of a plan.
examples: The strike cripples the city's transport.
High prices cripple small businesses.

usage.pos: verb / noun (plural, offensive when used about people)

meaning: A time of great danger, difficulty or confusion
trick: CRISIS: things are CRASHING.
examples: The country is facing an economic crisis.
Stay calm in a crisis.

usage.pattern: in a crisis; a crisis of something

meaning: Hard, dry and easily broken (food); also fresh and cool (air); also clear and neat
trick: CRISP like a fresh potato CRISP.
examples: The apple was crisp and sweet.
It was a crisp, cold morning.

meaning: The part of the body or trousers between the legs
trick: CROTCH: where your trouser legs meet.
examples: His jeans ripped at the crotch.
The ball hit him in the crotch.

meaning: To bend your knees and lower your body close to the ground
trick: CROUCH: like a cat getting low, ready to pounce.
examples: Crouch down so they can't see you.
He crouched behind the car.

meaning: Bending the knees to get low to the ground
trick: CROUCHING like a tiger hiding in the grass.
examples: The cat was crouching behind the sofa.
He was crouching to tie his shoes.

meaning: Officially made king or queen; also named the best (past)
hindi: ताज पहनाया गया, राजा बनाया गया; सर्वश्रेष्ठ घोषित
trick: CROWNED: a CROWN was put on her head.
examples: She was crowned queen in 1953.
He was crowned the champion.

meaning: A pot for melting metals; also a difficult test that changes you
hindi: धातु गलाने की कुठाली; कठिन परीक्षा
trick: CRUCIBLE: a pot where things melt and change, like a hard test.
examples: The metal was melted in a crucible.
The war was the crucible of his character.

meaning: A very small piece of bread or cake; also a tiny amount
trick: CRUMB: a tiny bit left from a CRUMBLY biscuit.
examples: There were crumbs all over the table.
He didn't leave a crumb on his plate.

meaning: To break into small pieces; also to fall apart slowly
trick: CRUMBLE: biscuits fall into CRUMBS.
examples: The old wall began to crumble.
Their marriage started to crumble.

meaning: Crushed into untidy folds; also fell down suddenly (past)
hindi: मुड़ा-तुड़ा, मसला हुआ; अचानक गिर पड़ा
trick: CRUMPLED like a paper ball in your hand.
examples: He threw away the crumpled paper.
She crumpled to the floor in shock.

usage.pattern: crumple something (up); crumple to the floor

meaning: A stick that fits under your arm to help you walk; also something you depend on too much
trick: CRUTCH: you lean on it when your leg hurts.
examples: He walked with a crutch after the accident.
Coffee became her crutch.

usage.pattern: walk with a crutch; use something as a crutch

meaning: A pair of sticks that fit under your arms to help you walk
trick: One CRUTCH, two CRUTCHES: for a broken leg.
examples: She's on crutches after breaking her leg.
He walked slowly on his crutches.

usage.pattern: be on crutches; walk on crutches

meaning: Became clear and definite; also formed crystals (past)
hindi: स्पष्ट हो गया; क्रिस्टल बन गया
trick: CRYSTALLIZED: ideas became clear as CRYSTAL.
examples: Her plans crystallized after the trip.
The honey crystallized in the cold.

meaning: A long, green vegetable eaten raw in salads
trick: CUCUMBER: cool as a CUCUMBER.
examples: She added cucumber to the salad.
He stayed as cool as a cucumber.

usage.pattern: slice a cucumber; cool as a cucumber

meaning: A signal for someone to do something; also the stick used in snooker and pool
trick: CUE = a Queue signal: 'your turn now'.
examples: When the music stops, that's your cue to enter.
He picked up the cue and hit the ball.

usage.pattern: on cue; take your cue from someone

meaning: The end part of a sleeve near the wrist; also a light hit with the hand
hindi: कफ़, आस्तीन का सिरा; हल्का थप्पड़
trick: CUFF: the end of your sleeve with a button.
examples: There's a stain on your shirt cuff.
She gave him a cuff on the head.

meaning: Sleeve ends near the wrist; also (informal) handcuffs
trick: CUFFS: sleeve ends, or police HANDCUFFS.
examples: Roll up your cuffs before washing.
The police put him in cuffs.

usage.pattern: in cuffs; roll up your cuffs

meaning: Reached the final or highest point after a long process (past)
trick: CULMINATED: reached the summit, the very top.
examples: Years of practice culminated in a gold medal.
The festival culminated with fireworks.

meaning: Growing crops or plants; also developing a skill or quality
trick: CULTIVATE the land, CULTIVATION of crops.
examples: The cultivation of rice needs lots of water.
Reading helps the cultivation of the mind.

meaning: Increasing step by step as more is added
trick: CUMULATIVE: it ACCUMULATES.
examples: The cumulative effect of stress is harmful.
Your cumulative score is 85.

meaning: To control or limit something; also the edge of a pavement (US spelling of kerb)
hindi: रोक लगाना, नियंत्रित करना; फुटपाथ का किनारा
trick: CURB your temper, like a CURB stops the car.
examples: We need to curb our spending.
He parked close to the curb.

meaning: A rule that people must be home or indoors by a certain time
trick: CURFEW: a CURE for late nights.
examples: My curfew is 10 p.m.
The city set a curfew after the riots.

usage.pattern: a curfew (of a time); break curfew

meaning: Decorative curls or twists in writing or design (plural)
trick: CURLI-CUES: little CURLS.
examples: Her handwriting has pretty curlicues.
The gate had iron curlicues.

meaning: The subjects taught in a school or course
trick: CURRICULUM: the race COURSE of school subjects.
examples: Maths is part of the school curriculum.
The new curriculum includes coding.

meaning: Handwriting where the letters are joined together
trick: CURSIVE: letters RUN together (like 'course').
examples: Kids learn to write in cursive.
Her cursive is beautiful.

meaning: A soft pillow for a chair or sofa; also something that reduces a shock
trick: CUSHION: a soft pillow on the sofa.
examples: Put a cushion behind your back.
Savings give you a cushion in hard times.

usage.pattern: a cushion against something; cushion the blow/fall

meaning: Soft pillows for chairs or sofas (plural)
trick: One CUSHION, many CUSHIONS on the sofa.
examples: The sofa has lots of soft cushions.
She threw the cushions on the floor.

meaning: The point where one thing is about to change into another
trick: On the CUSP: at the edge, about to tip over.
examples: She is on the cusp of a big career.
We're on the cusp of winter.

meaning: A shape cut out of paper or card; also a device that stops a machine
hindi: काटकर बनाई आकृति; स्वचालित बंद करने वाला यंत्र
trick: CUT-OUT: CUT it OUT of paper.
examples: The kids made paper cutouts of stars.
There was a cardboard cutout of the actor.

meaning: A creature that is part human and part machine (science fiction)
trick: CYBORG = CYBernetic ORGanism: half human, half robot.
examples: The film is about a cyborg from the future.
He dressed as a cyborg for the party.
